normalized_review.doc:
Job tracker rules (for my own application spreadsheet)

The tracker should give every application exactly one next step.

Quick context: I apply to a lot of roles, so old postings pile up fast.

If the posting is more than 30 days old, mark it stale.

Anything at one of my top companies stays active.

If it's been over 3 weeks and I haven't heard back, send a follow-up, but only for postings that aren't stale and aren't at a top company. For top companies I follow up myself, so the tracker shouldn't.

Otherwise, just wait.

The only facts the tracker knows are: is the posting over 30 days old (yes/no), is it a top company (yes/no), has it been over 3 weeks since I applied (yes/no), and have I heard back (yes/no).

normalized_review.doc:
Package room rules for our building

Each package gets one action when it's logged at the desk.

Honestly most of these are just Amazon boxes, but we have to be consistent.

If it's perishable and the resident is away, return it to the sender.

If it's perishable and the resident is home, notify the resident right away.

For anything that isn't perishable: if it needs a signature, hold it at the front desk.

Non-perishable packages that don't need a signature go in a locker, unless they're oversized. Oversized ones get held at the desk too.

The desk only knows: is it perishable (yes/no), is the resident away (yes/no), does it need a signature (yes/no), and is it oversized (yes/no).
